newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber ends mixed on currency adjustment.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber ends mixed on currency adjustment.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed on Monday with the market adjusting itself to a further weakening of the ringgit, dealers said.
"It has to be the currency...there's nothing else apparent," said a trader.
Dealers did not report any business for the day, adding that volumes were thin at best.
The ringgit was trading at 2.7880 to a dollar at 0800 GMT in Kuala Lumpur on Monday, from 2.7680 at 0200 GMT.
In the rubber market, the RSS1 for September buyer closed at 251.50 cents (90 cents U.S.), up one cent from Friday.
The SMR20 for September buyer was quoted half-cent down at 249.50 cents a kg.

Traders said at midday that buyers could be looking at the Jakarta rubber market because the rupiah had fallen more drastically than the ringgit since last week, making prices of Indonesian rubber more attractive.
Traders in Kuala Lumpur were offering the SMR 20 at 249 cents a kg, the SMR CV at 289 cents, SMR L at 270, SMR 5 at 262, SMR 10 at 250 and drum latex at 192 for Aug/Sept.
The INRO five-day indicator was at 192.41 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on Aug 15 from 192.18 on Aug 14. The daily price was at 192.47 from 192.73 previously.
